title: Tunnawiya’s Ritual for the Royal Couple
eyebrow: CTH 409.II · litanies of the twelve limbs

dating.label: copy c. 14th–13th c. BCE
dating.note: KUB 9.34 is catalogued as a New Hittite (NS) manuscript; the script date does not fix when the ritual was composed.

purpose: A healing ritual for a king and queen that removes sickness, curses and the 'tongues' of every kind of person from the patient's twelve limbs.
attribution: Attributed to Tunnawiya, the Old Woman
sourceSummary: KUB 9.34 (Bo 2385) · CTH 409.II, second tablet, not complete

phases.name: Naming the harms
phases.idea: Litanies name the afflictions, tongues and causes lodged in the patient.

phases.name: Fitting the limbs and the ram
phases.idea: The twelve limbs are fitted and a ram's twelve limbs take up their sickness.

phases.name: Pulling out and holding over
phases.idea: Harm is pulled out, carriers are held over back and chest, and the patient spits into a sheep.

phases.name: Piglets and the divine search
phases.idea: Live and dough piglets, myths of divine search, and a final removal litany.

steps.title: Name the afflictions of the patient
steps.shortDescription: The Old Woman recites a list of afflictions of head, soul, bones and inner parts, and of the year and month.
steps.summary: The Old Woman recites a list of afflictions of head, soul, bones and inner parts, and of the year and month.
steps.evidence: KUB 9.34 Vs. I 20′–Vs. I 24′. The opening of the utterance is broken and the verb 'has (not) overcome' is uncertain in sense; the list continues with KI.MIN ('ditto') entries in ¶5.

image.alt: Name the afflictions of the patient
image.note: Only what the paragraph states is depicted; dress and posture are illustrative.

atoms.time: of the year and of the month

steps.title: Name the tongues of every kind of person
steps.shortDescription: The litany lists the 'tongues' (slander, curse) of palace attendants, priests, troops, mountain folk, the dead and the living, and of sorcery.
steps.summary: The litany lists the 'tongues' (slander, curse) of palace attendants, priests, troops, mountain folk, the dead and the living, and of sorcery.
steps.evidence: KUB 9.34 Vs. II 3–Vs. II 11. Parallel lists in ¶¶6–7; many social groups are named (lulaḫi-, ḫapiru-men, šarikuwa-troops).

image.alt: Name the tongues of every kind of person
image.note: Only what the paragraph states is depicted; dress and posture are illustrative.

the tongue of the dead and of the living

steps.title: Recount how the harm was picked up
steps.shortDescription: Naming the patient, she lists possible ways he picked up harm: on a road, by seeing, by stepping on something.
steps.summary: Naming the patient, she lists possible ways he picked up harm: on a road, by seeing, by stepping on something.
steps.evidence: KUB 9.34 Vs. II 12–Vs. II 17. The alternatives are introduced by 'See, (either)… or…'; one alternative is broken.

image.alt: Recount how the harm was picked up
image.note: Only what the paragraph states is depicted; dress and posture are illustrative.

about.label: something brought back from a road

steps.title: Name the patient's evil speech against the gods
steps.shortDescription: The list continues with impurity, sorcery, strife and the patient's speaking against the gods with an evil mouth.
steps.summary: The list continues with impurity, sorcery, strife and the patient's speaking against the gods with an evil mouth.
steps.evidence: KUB 9.34 Vs. II 18–Vs. II 19. Beginning broken. Classed as confession because it names the patient's own offence against the gods; the speaker is the practitioner on his behalf.

image.note: Only what the paragraph states is depicted; dress and posture are illustrative.

steps.title: Fit the twelve limbs together
steps.shortDescription: A litany declares each body part fitted to its counterpart: ear to ear, hand to hands, foot to foot, blood to blood.
steps.phase: Fitting the limbs and the ram
steps.summary: A litany declares each body part fitted to its counterpart: ear to ear, hand to hands, foot to foot, blood to blood.
steps.evidence: KUB 9.34 Vs. II 28–Vs. II 34. Continues ¶12 (ear, upper arm, hand, nails). Whether the 'fitting' refers to the patient's limbs or to a matching of patient and animal limbs is unclear.

image.alt: Fit the twelve limbs together
image.note: Only what the paragraph states is depicted; dress and posture are illustrative.

steps.title: Cut up the ram's twelve limbs
steps.shortDescription: The twelve limbs of a ram are cut up for the patient.
steps.phase: Fitting the limbs and the ram
steps.summary: The twelve limbs of a ram are cut up for the patient.
steps.evidence: KUB 9.34 Vs. II 35–Vs. II 37. The verb is restored ('cut up(?)'); killing is not stated in the surviving text.

image.alt: Cut up the ram's twelve limbs
image.note: Only what the paragraph states is depicted; dress and posture are illustrative.

steps.title: Let each ram limb take up the sickness of the same limb
steps.shortDescription: Limb by limb, the ram's parts are told to take up the sickness of the patient's matching parts: head, shoulder, finger, rib.
steps.phase: Fitting the limbs and the ram
steps.summary: Limb by limb, the ram's parts are told to take up the sickness of the patient's matching parts: head, shoulder, finger, rib.
steps.evidence: KUB 9.34 Vs. II 38–Vs. II 41. ¶14 adds that 'they demand(?) the sickness of the limbs of this man'; the list continues in ¶16.

image.alt: Let each ram limb take up the sickness of the same limb
image.note: Only what the paragraph states is depicted; dress and posture are illustrative.

steps.title: Declare the harm pulled out
steps.shortDescription: The Old Woman declares that she has pulled the harm out of him from the right.
steps.summary: The Old Woman declares that she has pulled the harm out of him from the right.
steps.evidence: KUB 9.34 Rs. III 5′–Rs. III 12′. Parallel 'I pulled (it) out' in fragmentary ¶18.

image.alt: Declare the harm pulled out
image.note: Only what the paragraph states is depicted; dress and posture are illustrative.

steps.title: Take the evil fright from him
steps.shortDescription: She takes the evil fright away from the patient.
steps.summary: She takes the evil fright away from the patient.
steps.evidence: KUB 9.34 Rs. III 5′–Rs. III 12′. No object or instrument is named; the removal may be gestural.

image.alt: Take the evil fright from him
image.note: Only what the paragraph states is depicted; dress and posture are illustrative.

steps.title: Conjure around the twelve limbs
steps.shortDescription: She takes up the incantation again and goes around the twelve limbs in the same way.
steps.summary: She takes up the incantation again and goes around the twelve limbs in the same way.
steps.evidence: KUB 9.34 Rs. III 5′–Rs. III 12′. Refers back to the limb litany (¶¶12–16).

image.alt: Conjure around the twelve limbs
image.note: Only what the paragraph states is depicted; dress and posture are illustrative.

steps.title: Hold it over his back
steps.shortDescription: The patient lies down in another position and she holds (the carrier) over his back while conjuring the same words.
steps.summary: The patient lies down in another position and she holds (the carrier) over his back while conjuring the same words.
steps.evidence: KUB 9.34 Rs. III 5′–Rs. III 12′. The held object is not named; the context before the gap (ram limbs, pig) leaves it uncertain.

image.alt: Hold it over his back
image.note: The object is not named in the text; it is shown as an indistinct bundle.

steps.title: Hold a sheep over his chest
steps.shortDescription: The patient lies down again and she holds a sheep over his chest.
steps.summary: The patient lies down again and she holds a sheep over his chest.
steps.evidence: KUB 9.34 Rs. III 13′–Rs. III 15′. Reuses unit tunnawiya-hold-black-sheep (KUB 7.53+): same act and principal object, a sheep held over the patient. Colour is not stated here.

image.alt: Hold a sheep over his chest
image.note: The reused image shows a black sheep; KUB 9.34 does not state the colour.

steps.title: Compare the patient to a field ploughed again
steps.shortDescription: As a field is ploughed a third and fourth time, so she treats this person a third and fourth time.
steps.summary: As a field is ploughed a third and fourth time, so she treats this person a third and fourth time.
steps.evidence: KUB 9.34 Rs. III 16′–Rs. III 17′.

image.alt: Compare the patient to a field ploughed again
image.note: Only what the paragraph states is depicted; dress and posture are illustrative.

steps.title: Conjure around the limbs again
steps.shortDescription: With the sheep, she repeats the incantation around the twelve limbs.
steps.summary: With the sheep, she repeats the incantation around the twelve limbs.
steps.evidence: KUB 9.34 Rs. III 18′–Rs. III 19′.

image.alt: Conjure around the limbs again

steps.title: Spit into the sheep's mouth
steps.shortDescription: The sheep is held out to the patient and he spits twice into its mouth.
steps.summary: The sheep is held out to the patient and he spits twice into its mouth.
steps.evidence: KUB 9.34 Rs. III 20′–Rs. III 23′. 'it' is most likely the sheep of ¶20, marked (?) in the translation. 'release' is used as the closest verb for spitting out.

image.alt: Spit into the sheep's mouth
image.note: Only what the paragraph states is depicted; dress and posture are illustrative.

steps.title: Command him to spit out the harms
steps.shortDescription: She orders him to spit out the āḫra-, the waḫra-, the anger of the gods and the tongue of the multitude.
steps.summary: She orders him to spit out the āḫra-, the waḫra-, the anger of the gods and the tongue of the multitude.
steps.evidence: KUB 9.34 Rs. III 20′–Rs. III 23′. āḫra- and waḫra- are untranslated.

steps.summary: A piglet of dough and a live piglet are brought.

steps.summary: The live piglet is repeatedly swung away (from the patient?).
steps.evidence: KUB 9.34 Rs. III 24′–Rs. III 27′. Not matched to tunnawiya-hold-piglet: the live pig is swung 'away(?)' rather than held over the patient; direction uncertain.

steps.title: Tell of the great god driving from Landa
steps.shortDescription: She tells how the great god drove from Landa, and names those who frightened and agitated him.
steps.summary: She tells how the great god drove from Landa, and names those who frightened and agitated him.
steps.evidence: KUB 9.34 Rs. III 28′–Rs. III 32′. A mythic narrative (historiola); much of the wording is obscure.

steps.shortDescription: She speaks the name of the person she is treating.
steps.summary: She speaks the name of the person she is treating.
steps.evidence: KUB 9.34 Rs. III 28′–Rs. III 32′. The name is not given; ¶30 repeats the instruction.

steps.title: Tell of the gods' search of his body
steps.shortDescription: A narrative: the angry Sun-god sends the Ilaliyant-deities; the searchers see the patient's eyebrow, eyelashes and twelve limbs.
steps.summary: A narrative: the angry Sun-god sends the Ilaliyant-deities; the searchers see the patient's eyebrow, eyelashes and twelve limbs.
steps.evidence: KUB 9.34 Rs. III 33′–Rs. III 42′. The Sun-god is agent within the story, not an addressee. The closing 'it became sweet(?) inside him(?)' is uncertain.

image.note: Only what the paragraph states is depicted; dress and posture are illustrative.

steps.title: Cut them off from the limbs
steps.shortDescription: In the myth the Mother-goddess smears karšikarši- before the evil gods, and the command sounds: cut them off from eyebrows, eyelashes and the twelve limbs.
steps.summary: In the myth the Mother-goddess smears karšikarši- before the evil gods, and the command sounds: cut them off from eyebrows, eyelashes and the twelve limbs.
steps.evidence: KUB 9.34 Rs. III 43′–Rs. IV 3′. Speaker within the narrative is the evil šiwanni- (?); what is cut off is unstated (likely the evil gods' hold).

image.note: Only what the paragraph states is depicted; dress and posture are illustrative.

steps.title: Let her remove the tongues
steps.shortDescription: A litany asks that she remove the shortened year, the anger of the gods, and the tongues of every class of people.
steps.summary: A litany asks that she remove the shortened year, the anger of the gods, and the tongues of every class of people.
steps.evidence: KUB 9.34 Rs. IV 7′–Rs. IV 18′. Begins in ¶27 and continues through ¶28; the remover is probably the Mother-goddess.
